peers.name: ICICI PRU LIFE INS CO LTD

bull_bear.body:
- Scale and share in Indian non-life: "The market share of the Company on GWP stood at 3.4% as compared to 3.3% for the previous financial year."
- Capital strength relative to the regulatory floor: IRDAI requires a minimum solvency of 1.5 times, and "The solvency position of the Company as at March 31, 2026 was 2.42 times as compared to 2.24 times as at March 31, 2025."
- Diversified multi-line book across Fire, Motor, Engineering and Health, Travel & Personal Accident plus other lines of business, rather than a single-line insurer
- Broad multi-channel distribution — individual agents, corporate agents (banks/FII/HFC and others), insurance brokers, MISP, insurance marketing firms and point-of-sales persons
- Continuity of the "DIGIT" / "GO DIGIT" brand: the Board is satisfied that the new brand licence arrangement "ensures continuity of brand usage and does not have any adverse impact on the Company's operations, business continuity, or brand positioning"
- Governance architecture with a Board of nine directors of which five are Independent — "more than half of the Board consists of Independent Directors" and "The roles of the Chairman and the MD & CEO are distinct and separate."
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Line-of-business concentration in Motor — The Board's Report states that out of the Company's total GWP, "Motor 59.9%", with Fire 9.7%, Engineering 2.0%, Health, Travel & Personal Accident 18.3% and other lines 10.1% — so a majority of the book, and its pricing, third-party liability and claims experience, sits in a single regulated line.
- Underwriting result remains loss-making at the combined-ratio level and widened during the year — "The combined ratio of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 was 110.7% as against 109.3% for the previous financial year", i.e. claims plus expenses continued to exceed premium and the ratio deteriorated year-on-year, while the loss ratio was broadly flat at 72.9% versus 72.8%.
- Regulatory solvency floor constrains growth and capital flexibility — "IRDAI requires insurance companies to maintain a minimum solvency of 1.5 times which is calculated in a manner as specified in the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024"; the Company stood at 2.42 times as at March 31, 2026 versus 2.24 times a year earlier, so premium growth is permanently tied to maintaining regulatory capital.
- Execution and approval risk on the proposed amalgamation of the holding company — The Scheme is "conditional upon receipt of observation/no-objection letters from the Stock Exchanges", approval by the requisite majority of each class of creditors and members, votes in favour exceeding those against, "approvals from the Competition Commission of India and the IRDAI under the Insurance Act, 1938" and sanction by the NCLT — a multi-regulator chain with no stated completion date, and the Appointed Date is itself the Effective Date.
- Brand is owned outside the Company and used under licence — "the trademarks and brand names 'DIGIT' and 'GO DIGIT', together with other related trademarks central to the Company's business and brand identity, were assigned by Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited ('the holding Company') to Go Digit Solutions Private Limited, a Promoter Group entity"; the earlier licence was terminated and a new licence executed, so the Company's core brand right is contractual and rests with a promoter-group party.
- Reduced net retention increases dependence on reinsurance arrangements — "The net retention ratio and the net earning ratio ... were 73.7% and 101.1% respectively as against 80.0% and 97.8% respectively for the previous financial year" — a lower retention ratio means a larger share of risk is ceded, making outcomes more dependent on reinsurer capacity, pricing and recoveries.
- Growth is tied to a single industry and geography whose own growth is cyclical — "The industry's Gross Direct Premium ('GDP') grew from ₹ 3,07,66,069 Lakhs in FY2024-25 to ₹ 3,36,12,268 Lakhs in FY2025-26, marking a growth of 9.3%" — the Company writes general insurance in India only, with market share of 3.4% versus 3.3%, so its top line moves with Indian non-life industry growth and share shifts.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Go Digit General Insurance Limited carries on general (non-life) insurance business in India, and there was no change in the nature of the business carried on during the year. Its book spans Fire, Motor (own damage and third party), Engineering, and Health, Travel & Personal Accident, alongside other miscellaneous lines such as Workmen Compensation, liability, Aviation and Crop. Business is sourced through a multi-channel network of individual agents, corporate agents (banks/FII/HFC and others), insurance brokers, motor insurance service providers (MISP) and point-of-sales persons, and the Company uses the "GO DIGIT" brand under a licence from a Promoter Group entity.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Build a business that combines technology, disciplined underwriting and customer relevance as the Company enters its second decade of operations, on the belief that insurers that stay simple, nimble and agile will be best placed to serve India's opportunity
- Strengthen underwriting discipline and claims rigour without compromising customer centricity — "staying disciplined in underwriting, prudent in capital allocation, sharper in execution, and unwavering in the customer experience we deliver"
- Use technology and AI to reduce friction across the policy buying, renewal and claims journey, and keep strengthening the technology backbone so that reliability and speed scale with the business
- Grow through the partner ecosystem — equipping 81,124 partners with technology, tailored solutions, real-time insights and self-service capabilities so selling, servicing and claims are more seamless
- Agility as an operating model: sense change early, enter new areas and build solutions for emerging risks, illustrated by climate-linked parametric insurance including heat-based protection for migrant labourers and moisture index-based protection for farmers
- Transparency as a discipline — track and publicly disclose customer-facing process speed through a bi-annual Transparency Report
- Future-readiness on reporting — a full year of parallel Ind AS reporting was completed ahead of the mandatory transition from April 1, 2026
- People and culture: 4,800+ "Simplifiers" operating under the OPEN (Ownership, People Relations, Evolve and Engage, No Hierarchy) culture across 100+ offices in 28 states and UTs
- CSR focused on education and skilling, digital literacy, healthcare access, youth development and sustainable community infrastructure across 11 locations
- The BRSR sustainability information for FY2025-26 was subject to an independent REASONABLE assurance engagement (the higher assurance level) by PKF Sridhar & Santhanam LLP, conducted under SSAE 3000 and SAE 3410, with an unmodified opinion that the Identified Sustainability Information is prepared in all material respects in accordance with the BRSR Criteria
- Climate/energy footprint is within the assured indicator set (P6-E1): total energy consumed, total energy consumed from renewable sources and the % of energy from renewable sources, energy intensity per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and energy intensity per headcount
- GHG footprint is within the assured indicator set (P6-E7): total Scope 1 emissions, total Scope 2 emissions, and Scope 1+2 emission intensity both per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and per headcount
- Water footprint is within the assured indicator set (P6-E3 and P6-E4): total water consumption in kilolitres, water intensity per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and per headcount, and water discharge by destination and level of treatment
- Circularity/waste is within the assured indicator set (P6-E9): total weight of waste generated, waste intensity per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and per headcount, and, for each waste category, waste recovered through recycling/re-use and waste disposed by disposal method
- Employee wellbeing and safety are assured (P3-E1(c) and P3-E11): spending on measures towards well-being of employees and workers, Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate per one million person-hours worked, total recordable work-related injuries and number of fatalities
- Gender diversity and workplace conduct are assured (P5-E3(b) and P5-E7): gross wages paid to females as a % of total wages paid by the entity, and complaints filed under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
- Business-conduct concentration disclosures are assured (P1-E8 and P1-E9): days of accounts payable, and concentration of purchases and sales with trading houses, dealers and related parties together with loans, advances and investments with related parties
- Assurance scope limitation to note: it excludes data for factors not under the Company's operational control, information outside April 2025-March 2026 and comparatives, and "statements that describe the expression of opinion, belief, aspiration, expectation, aim or future intentions provided by the Company"
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or capex programme — Go Digit is an asset-light general insurer and the Board's Report records that "There has been no change in the business carried on by the Company during the year" and that "There have been no material changes or commitments, affecting the financial position of the Company which have occurred between the end of financial year of the Company and the date of this report." The only structural corporate action described is a proposed amalgamation: on December 19, 2025 the Board approved a scheme of amalgamation of the holding company, Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited (GDISPL), into the Company under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, in consideration for which the Company will issue fully paid-up equity shares to GDISPL's equity and preference shareholders while GDISPL's shareholding in the Company is cancelled and GDISPL is dissolved without winding up. The Appointed Date is the Effective Date, being the last of the dates on which certified copies of the NCLT sanction orders are filed with the Registrar of Companies, Pune; the Scheme is conditional on stock-exchange observation/no-objection letters, approval by the requisite majority of each class of creditors and members, and approvals from the Competition Commission of India, IRDAI and the NCLT — so no completion timeline is stated. Management's stated rationale is simplification of the structure, reduction of shareholding tiers and administrative overheads, enabling shareholders to contribute to the Transferee Company's capital infusion needs and growth objectives, and a leaner holding structure aligned with regulatory intent. Separately, a brand assignment moved the "DIGIT" and "GO DIGIT" trademarks from the holding company to Go Digit Solutions Private Limited, a Promoter Group entity, and a new brand licence agreement was executed under which the Company continues to enjoy uninterrupted and similar rights to use the brand for its insurance business in India. On the operating side, the Chairman frames future capacity in terms of readiness rather than assets — a full year of parallel Ind AS reporting was completed ahead of the mandatory transition from April 1, 2026, and the improved solvency ratio is described as "keeping us well positioned for future growth".
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- "India's insurance opportunity remains structurally underpenetrated and significant. Regulatory reforms, digital adoption, and increasing risk awareness are continuing to expand the category in meaningful ways."
- Industry momentum improved — "the Indian non-life insurance sector gained momentum in FY2025-26. Gross direct premium income crossed ₹3.5 trillion, and growth improved to 9.3% from 6.2% last year."
- "Reforms such as 100% foreign direct investment in the coming years could support greater capital and competition" — a driver of both capital availability and competitive intensity
- "the launch of much-anticipated Bima Sugam truly has the potential to reset the industry's operating model through simplicity and scale"
- IRDAI's reform push is "increasingly aligned towards the mission of 'Insurance for All by 2047'", with penetration in India still low
- Quality of growth, not just volume, is management's stated frame — "we are equally clear that the quality of growth will continue to matter for insurers"
- The year was "marked by regulatory transition, competitive intensity and various macro factors", set against a global environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, changing trade policies and financial-market volatility while India remained one of the better growth stories supported by domestic demand and policy push
- Cost efficiency as a margin lever — "our management expenses to GWP remained among the most efficient in the industry"
- Capital position supports growth — "our solvency ratio improved to 2.42x from 2.24x, keeping us well positioned for future growth"

currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or capex programme — Go Digit is an asset-light general insurer and the Board's Report records that "There has been no change in the business carried on by the Company during the year" and that "There have been no material changes or commitments, affecting the financial position of the Company which have occurred between the end of financial year of the Company and the date of this report." The only structural corporate action described is a proposed amalgamation: on December 19, 2025 the Board approved a scheme of amalgamation of the holding company, Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited (GDISPL), into the Company under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, in consideration for which the Company will issue fully paid-up equity shares to GDISPL's equity and preference shareholders while GDISPL's shareholding in the Company is cancelled and GDISPL is dissolved without winding up. The Appointed Date is the Effective Date, being the last of the dates on which certified copies of the NCLT sanction orders are filed with the Registrar of Companies, Pune; the Scheme is conditional on stock-exchange observation/no-objection letters, approval by the requisite majority of each class of creditors and members, and approvals from the Competition Commission of India, IRDAI and the NCLT — so no completion timeline is stated. Management's stated rationale is simplification of the structure, reduction of shareholding tiers and administrative overheads, enabling shareholders to contribute to the Transferee Company's capital infusion needs and growth objectives, and a leaner holding structure aligned with regulatory intent. Separately, a brand assignment moved the "DIGIT" and "GO DIGIT" trademarks from the holding company to Go Digit Solutions Private Limited, a Promoter Group entity, and a new brand licence agreement was executed under which the Company continues to enjoy uninterrupted and similar rights to use the brand for its insurance business in India. On the operating side, the Chairman frames future capacity in terms of readiness rather than assets — a full year of parallel Ind AS reporting was completed ahead of the mandatory transition from April 1, 2026, and the improved solvency ratio is described as "keeping us well positioned for future growth".

risks.note: The Board's Report states that out of the Company's total GWP, "Motor 59.9%", with Fire 9.7%, Engineering 2.0%, Health, Travel & Personal Accident 18.3% and other lines 10.1% — so a majority of the book, and its pricing, third-party liability and claims experience, sits in a single regulated line.

risks.risk: Underwriting result remains loss-making at the combined-ratio level and widened during the year
risks.note: "The combined ratio of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 was 110.7% as against 109.3% for the previous financial year", i.e. claims plus expenses continued to exceed premium and the ratio deteriorated year-on-year, while the loss ratio was broadly flat at 72.9% versus 72.8%.

risks.risk: Regulatory solvency floor constrains growth and capital flexibility
risks.note: "IRDAI requires insurance companies to maintain a minimum solvency of 1.5 times which is calculated in a manner as specified in the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024"; the Company stood at 2.42 times as at March 31, 2026 versus 2.24 times a year earlier, so premium growth is permanently tied to maintaining regulatory capital.

risks.risk: Execution and approval risk on the proposed amalgamation of the holding company
risks.note: The Scheme is "conditional upon receipt of observation/no-objection letters from the Stock Exchanges", approval by the requisite majority of each class of creditors and members, votes in favour exceeding those against, "approvals from the Competition Commission of India and the IRDAI under the Insurance Act, 1938" and sanction by the NCLT — a multi-regulator chain with no stated completion date, and the Appointed Date is itself the Effective Date.

risks.risk: Brand is owned outside the Company and used under licence
risks.note: "the trademarks and brand names 'DIGIT' and 'GO DIGIT', together with other related trademarks central to the Company's business and brand identity, were assigned by Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited ('the holding Company') to Go Digit Solutions Private Limited, a Promoter Group entity"; the earlier licence was terminated and a new licence executed, so the Company's core brand right is contractual and rests with a promoter-group party.

risks.risk: Reduced net retention increases dependence on reinsurance arrangements
risks.note: "The net retention ratio and the net earning ratio ... were 73.7% and 101.1% respectively as against 80.0% and 97.8% respectively for the previous financial year" — a lower retention ratio means a larger share of risk is ceded, making outcomes more dependent on reinsurer capacity, pricing and recoveries.

risks.risk: Growth is tied to a single industry and geography whose own growth is cyclical
risks.note: "The industry's Gross Direct Premium ('GDP') grew from ₹ 3,07,66,069 Lakhs in FY2024-25 to ₹ 3,36,12,268 Lakhs in FY2025-26, marking a growth of 9.3%" — the Company writes general insurance in India only, with market share of 3.4% versus 3.3%, so its top line moves with Indian non-life industry growth and share shifts.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Go Digit General Insurance is an Indian non-life insurer writing a multi-line book led by Motor, with a roughly 3.4% share of industry gross written premium in FY2025-26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Go Digit General Insurance Limited carries on general (non-life) insurance business in India, and there was no change in the nature of the business carried on during the year. Its book spans Fire, Motor (own damage and third party), Engineering, and Health, Travel & Personal Accident, alongside other miscellaneous lines such as Workmen Compensation, liability, Aviation and Crop. Business is sourced through a multi-channel network of individual agents, corporate agents (banks/FII/HFC and others), insurance brokers, motor insurance service providers (MISP) and point-of-sales persons, and the Company uses the "GO DIGIT" brand under a licence from a Promoter Group entity.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Go Digit Infoworks Services Private Limited — related party: Holding company and company in which a director is interested; transaction categories disclosed are FMS and technology service charges, reimbursement of expenses, reimbursement of IPO expenses, purchase of fixed assets, policies issued, ESOP cost allocation and seat-sharing recovery. Kamesh Goyal holds another office in this entity.
- Go Digit Life Insurance Limited — related party: Promoter Group Company; an entity in which KMP are interested — Kamesh Goyal, Non-Executive Director, holds equity shares through Oben Ventures LLP. Transaction categories are group term life insurance premium, reimbursement of expenses, seat-sharing recovery, policies issued and reimbursement of commission on combi products incurred on behalf of Digit Life. Also an other-office/directorship of Kamesh Goyal, Gopalakrishnan Soundarajan, Michael Wallace, Vandana Gupta, Christof Mascher and Mukul Kant Gupta.
- Valueattics Reinsurance Limited — related party: Promoter Group Company; Kamesh Goyal, Non-Executive Director, holds equity shares through Oben Ventures LLP. Reinsurance counterparty — transaction categories are premium cession, commission paid, premium receipt, RI commission received, claims recoverable, FMS cost seat-sharing and GMC/GPA policies issued. Also an other-office of Kamesh Goyal, Gopalakrishnan Soundarajan, Michael Wallace and Mahender Kumar Garg.
- Go Digit Solutions Private Limited — related party: Promoter Group Company where Kamesh Goyal holds more than 2% shareholding; brand licence counterparty (brand licence cost). Also an other-office held by Kamesh Goyal and Gopalakrishnan Soundarajan.
- Oben Ventures LLP — related party: LLP in which Kamesh Goyal is a designated partner and through which he holds equity in Go Digit Life Insurance Limited and Valueattics Reinsurance Limited; transaction category disclosed is reimbursement of expenses.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fire:** Fire
- **Marine:** Marine Cargo, Marine Other
- **Motor:** Motor Own Damage (OD), Motor Third Party (TP)
- **Engineering:** Engineering
- **Health, Travel & Personal Accident:** Health, Travel, Personal Accident
- **Other miscellaneous lines:** Workmen Compensation, Public Liability, Product Liability, Aviation, Crop, Others

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body: India — the Company carries on its insurance business in India; the schedules show business written and claims paid in India, with nil outside India

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- "India's insurance opportunity remains structurally underpenetrated and significant. Regulatory reforms, digital adoption, and increasing risk awareness are continuing to expand the category in meaningful ways."
- Industry momentum improved — "the Indian non-life insurance sector gained momentum in FY2025-26. Gross direct premium income crossed ₹3.5 trillion, and growth improved to 9.3% from 6.2% last year."
- "Reforms such as 100% foreign direct investment in the coming years could support greater capital and competition" — a driver of both capital availability and competitive intensity
- "the launch of much-anticipated Bima Sugam truly has the potential to reset the industry's operating model through simplicity and scale"
- IRDAI's reform push is "increasingly aligned towards the mission of 'Insurance for All by 2047'", with penetration in India still low
- Quality of growth, not just volume, is management's stated frame — "we are equally clear that the quality of growth will continue to matter for insurers"
- The year was "marked by regulatory transition, competitive intensity and various macro factors", set against a global environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, changing trade policies and financial-market volatility while India remained one of the better growth stories supported by domestic demand and policy push
- Cost efficiency as a margin lever — "our management expenses to GWP remained among the most efficient in the industry"
- Capital position supports growth — "our solvency ratio improved to 2.42x from 2.24x, keeping us well positioned for future growth"

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build a business that combines technology, disciplined underwriting and customer relevance as the Company enters its second decade of operations, on the belief that insurers that stay simple, nimble and agile will be best placed to serve India's opportunity
- Strengthen underwriting discipline and claims rigour without compromising customer centricity — "staying disciplined in underwriting, prudent in capital allocation, sharper in execution, and unwavering in the customer experience we deliver"
- Use technology and AI to reduce friction across the policy buying, renewal and claims journey, and keep strengthening the technology backbone so that reliability and speed scale with the business
- Grow through the partner ecosystem — equipping 81,124 partners with technology, tailored solutions, real-time insights and self-service capabilities so selling, servicing and claims are more seamless
- Agility as an operating model: sense change early, enter new areas and build solutions for emerging risks, illustrated by climate-linked parametric insurance including heat-based protection for migrant labourers and moisture index-based protection for farmers
- Transparency as a discipline — track and publicly disclose customer-facing process speed through a bi-annual Transparency Report
- Future-readiness on reporting — a full year of parallel Ind AS reporting was completed ahead of the mandatory transition from April 1, 2026
- People and culture: 4,800+ "Simplifiers" operating under the OPEN (Ownership, People Relations, Evolve and Engage, No Hierarchy) culture across 100+ offices in 28 states and UTs
- CSR focused on education and skilling, digital literacy, healthcare access, youth development and sustainable community infrastructure across 11 locations
- The BRSR sustainability information for FY2025-26 was subject to an independent REASONABLE assurance engagement (the higher assurance level) by PKF Sridhar & Santhanam LLP, conducted under SSAE 3000 and SAE 3410, with an unmodified opinion that the Identified Sustainability Information is prepared in all material respects in accordance with the BRSR Criteria
- Climate/energy footprint is within the assured indicator set (P6-E1): total energy consumed, total energy consumed from renewable sources and the % of energy from renewable sources, energy intensity per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and energy intensity per headcount
- GHG footprint is within the assured indicator set (P6-E7): total Scope 1 emissions, total Scope 2 emissions, and Scope 1+2 emission intensity both per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and per headcount
- Water footprint is within the assured indicator set (P6-E3 and P6-E4): total water consumption in kilolitres, water intensity per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and per headcount, and water discharge by destination and level of treatment
- Circularity/waste is within the assured indicator set (P6-E9): total weight of waste generated, waste intensity per rupee of PPP-adjusted turnover and per headcount, and, for each waste category, waste recovered through recycling/re-use and waste disposed by disposal method
- Employee wellbeing and safety are assured (P3-E1(c) and P3-E11): spending on measures towards well-being of employees and workers, Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate per one million person-hours worked, total recordable work-related injuries and number of fatalities
- Gender diversity and workplace conduct are assured (P5-E3(b) and P5-E7): gross wages paid to females as a % of total wages paid by the entity, and complaints filed under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
- Business-conduct concentration disclosures are assured (P1-E8 and P1-E9): days of accounts payable, and concentration of purchases and sales with trading houses, dealers and related parties together with loans, advances and investments with related parties
- Assurance scope limitation to note: it excludes data for factors not under the Company's operational control, information outside April 2025-March 2026 and comparatives, and "statements that describe the expression of opinion, belief, aspiration, expectation, aim or future intentions provided by the Company"
